I-52.finding: Genealogy I records a boy of 4. Genealogy III's man has a wife, 249, and three children, 258 to 260. Both plates record the same fieldwork of 1918-19, so one name is carried by two people.

II-144.finding: Two Lizard girls of one name on one plate, a generation apart. II · 83 is the daughter of II · 27 Mini; II · 144, a generation below her, is the daughter of II · 119 Kʼăwaity˙id˙yuweʼ. Parsons separates them herself: she carries II · 83 over to Genealogy III as 222 and leaves II · 144 on Table 2 alone. Both are Lizard because descent is matrilineal and both mothers are Lizard — that is the rule holding, not evidence of identity.

II-182.finding: Nothing contradicts them: both F. and Sun, both generation 4, and a woman can be a wife on one plate and a daughter on another. But no relative of either is drawn on the other plate — not the husband, the eldest daughter, the parents or the sisters — so the name, the sex and the clan are the whole of the evidence, and this tool does not join on those alone.
